summary:
Zacatecas is a state of Mexico and stands under the national framework for passports, federal identity documents and federal criminal jurisdiction. The findings below are those specific to the state.

Zacatecas has a legislated administrative procedure for legal gender recognition. Deputies of the state's 64th Legislature approved a reform of the Family Code on gender identity on 23 December 2022 by 14 votes in favour to 7 against, after the Justice Committee issued a positive opinion on the measure. The reform establishes the possibility of issuing a new birth certificate recognising an applicant's gender identity, principally for the trans community. Zacatecas is not among the states identified as having no legislated gender-recognition procedure.

Implementation followed at the administrative level. In 2023 the director of the state Civil Registry issued guidelines giving effect to the law. Human Rights Watch's March 2025 state-by-state feature on legal gender recognition records both the 2022 Family Code reform and the 2023 Civil Registry guidelines for Zacatecas.

The state's criminal law carries its own protections. On 25 August 2021 the Congress of Zacatecas approved a prohibition and sanction on conversion therapies, known locally as ECOSIG, by adding fraction VI to article 182 Bis of the state Penal Code. Anyone who incites hatred or violence on grounds of sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or who promotes such practices, faces one to three years' imprisonment or up to 300 days of community work. The same session typified hate crimes motivated by sexual orientation and gender identity in the state Penal Code.

Recognition came later than those protections. A gender-identity initiative debated in the same 2021 session, alongside a constitutional and family-code reform, failed to obtain enough votes and remained pending; the gender-identity reform passed in December 2022.
tangentialFactors:
Gender recognition in Zacatecas runs through the Family Code and the state Civil Registry rather than through a court, while the prohibition on practices aimed at changing gender identity and the hate-crime motive for sexual orientation and gender identity sit in the state Penal Code. The two were enacted in different sessions, the criminal provisions in August 2021 and the recognition reform in December 2022.

The 2023 guidelines issued by the director of the state Civil Registry are the operative administrative text for applicants; the official state gazette is the publication channel for both the reform and the guidelines.
localsOnly:
Residents of Zacatecas obtain recognition through the state Civil Registry, which issues a new birth certificate under the guidelines its director issued in 2023. The December 2022 reform was framed principally for the trans community of the state.

The state Penal Code's protection against conversion practices and its hate-crime motive for sexual orientation and gender identity apply to conduct within Zacatecas, so residents who promote or incite such practices face prosecution in the state.
outOfScopeNotes:
The sources do not record how many applications the Zacatecas Civil Registry has received or granted, how long the procedure takes, or whether refusals have been reported.

No Zacatecas-specific figures are available for prosecutions under article 182 Bis fraction VI of the state Penal Code or for charges brought under the hate-crime provisions typified in 2021.

The inventory contains no Zacatecas-specific incidents or statistics on violence against trans people, and does not record whether the 2023 Civil Registry guidelines have been amended since issue.
